description: Agent Reliability: submit a service’s dependency disclosure with its listing or terms: the disclosure with the service and each upstream provider with its id, its name, each function that depends on it and the stated fallback (or none); the listing with the service and each provider it names with the functions it ties to it and the fallback it states. The signed report gives the disclosure and the listing, each listed provider paired with a disclosed provider by name with legal suffixes set aside, the dependent functions matched both ways provider by provider, and the fallback on each side, and counts them, and names a discrepant disclosure: a provider the listing names that the disclosure leaves out, a function the listing ties to a provider that the disclosure does not, a fallback the listing states where the disclosure states none, and another fallback than the listing states; then a disclosed provider, function or fallback the listing leaves out and another service, with the fix for each and what would change the verdict. No providers on either side, functions on one side only, or a fallback in the listing with nothing stated in the disclosure leaves the disclosure unverified. Functions and fallbacks read by their words, with none and no fallback read as no fallback. This reads a reliability disclosure against the buyer-facing listing: wever_subprocessor-evidence-check reads a data-processing subprocessor register, each processor’s name, purpose and location, against the agreement or subprocessor list for privacy diligence, and wever_risk-dependency-check reads what one planned action of the agent’s own relies on staying available or true, while the dependency check reads, upstream provider by provider, which of a service’s functions depend on it and the fallback stated, against what the listing or terms tell buyers. Verdict rely_dependency_discrepant, rely_dependency_partial, rely_dependency_unverified or rely_dependency_consistent. POST /api/rely-dependency-check. Reads the reliability records supplied in the call and returns a signed report with the verdict, the evidence read, the findings with their fixes, and what would change the verdict; it reads consistency between documents only: it never probes, pings or measures a live service or endpoint, computes no service credit and names no amount owed, verifies nothing with outside sources and judges no service’s actual reliability, only whether its records agree with each other and with what it advertises, and the records stay in the report, with no network request, fetch, message, payment or external write. Agent Reliability reads a service’s reliability records for consistency between documents: an uptime report, an error budget record, a failover arrangement, a dependency disclosure, a degradation behavior record, an incident history, a maintenance record and a periodic reliability report, each against the log, SLO, terms, listing, advertised behavior, buyer disclosure, policy or records it should agree with. Beside it, wever_endpoint-reliability-check and wever_endpoint-honesty-check probe one live endpoint at one moment for the Endpoint reliability page, and the DiligenceOps reads such as wever_sla-evidence-check and wever_status-evidence-check restate one document on its own, while this family connects to nothing and reads the records in the call against each other and against what the service advertises. Paid URL: 0.10 USDC per call on Base via x402 exact, with the shared 10 signed-wallet free calls per rolling 30 days. Bind X-Wever-Wallet-Proof to the exact JSON arguments and the tool route. Returns a report with an Ed25519 signed receipt. Contract: /api/agent-reliability-contract. Human page: https://weverlabs.com/agent-reliability/.
